communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: ODA Roles, Audit Logs, and Permission History for Carol Williams
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

I request records sufficient to show the ODA business functions, permissions, role assignments, and system activity associated with the CPS account assigned to Carol Williams (CJWilliams1@cps.edu) from March 1, 2022, through July 31, 2022.

Specifically, I request:

1. Records sufficient to show all ODA business functions, roles, permissions, access rights, and security groups assigned to that account.

2. Role-history, permission-history, and business-function assignment records showing assignments, modifications, removals, revocations, transfers, and effective dates.

3. Audit logs, activity logs, transaction logs, access logs, and change-history records identifying actions performed by that account.

4. Records sufficient to identify any administrator, supervisor, or other individual who requested, approved, authorized, implemented, modified, removed, or transferred any role, permission, or business function associated with that account.

5. Permission-change logs, administrator-change records, workflow records, approval records, tickets, or similar records reflecting changes to the account's permissions or authority.

6. Copies of records-retention schedules, retention policies, destruction schedules, or records-management policies applicable to ODA records, audit logs, role-history records, permission-history records, and administrator-change records.

FERPA Redactions

7. If responsive records contain information protected by FERPA or other student privacy laws, please redact only the protected student information and produce all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of the records. I am not requesting other students' educational records and will accept redacted copies where necessary.

No-Records Alternative

8. If any responsive records do not exist, have been deleted, destroyed, archived, or are no longer maintained, please provide records sufficient to identify:

A. whether such records were created or maintained;
B. the applicable retention schedule;
C. the date and authority for destruction or disposition;
D. the records custodian responsible for maintaining such records; and
E. any alternative records documenting the requested roles, permissions, approvals, assignments, or account activity.

9. If no responsive records exist, please provide written certification that no responsive records exist.

I request responsive records in electronic format, including Excel, CSV, PDF, database exports, or native audit-log format.

Kindly, 

Tina Pearson

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Tina Pearson

Specifically, I request:

communications.subject: DC Freedom of Information Act Request: Special Police Officer Commissions
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the DC Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

October 29, 2026
To: District of Columbia Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection
Re: Freedom of Information Act Request – Special Police Officer Commissions
Pursuant to the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act, D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et
seq. ("FOIA"), I, Tracy Siska, on behalf of myself and the Chicago Justice Project (the "Project"),
respectfully request copies of the public records listed below from the District of Columbia
Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection ("DLCP"), including records of the former
Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs ("DCRA") now held by the DLCP.
FOIA A
Please provide copies of all Documents submitted by any individual or corporation seeking the
commission of any individual as a special police officer under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official
Code § 5-129.02 (formerly § 4-114) for the years 2023 through 2025.
FOIA B
Please provide copies of all Documents, including but not limited to the commission issued to each
special police officer, created or maintained by the DLCP in connection with the applications
described in FOIA A of this request.
FOIA C
1. Records maintained by the DLCP that show, or are sufficient to show, the name(s) of any
database(s) containing data in any way related to FOIA A or FOIA B of this request.
2. The data dictionary(ies) for any database(s) identified in response to request C1.
3. All training materials for any database(s) identified in response to request C1.
4. Records that show, or are sufficient to show, the official name(s) of any database(s)
maintained by a third party, to which the DLCP has access, that contain data related to
special police officers.
5. The data dictionary(ies) for any database(s) identified in response to request C4.
6. All training materials for any database(s) identified in response to request C4.
7. All non-privileged case-level data from the database(s) identified in response to request C1
for the years 2023 through 2025. Please omit only such data, if any, that the law requires
be withheld.
8. Documents sufficient to identify or account for any data withheld from the case-level data
provided in response to request C7.
9. All non-privileged case-level data from the database(s) identified in response to request C4
for the years 2023 through 2025. Please omit only such data, if any, that the law requires
be withheld.
10. Documents sufficient to identify or account for any data withheld from the case-level data
provided in response to request C9.
FOIA D
Please provide copies of all complaints the DLCP received regarding the conduct of special police
officers for the years 2023 through 2025, and all Records created in response to those complaints,
including but not limited to investigative Records.
FOIA E
Please provide all Records related to the DLCP's revocation of the commission of any special
police officer appointed under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official Code § 5-129.02 (formerly §
4-114) during the years 2023 through 2025.
FOIA F
Please provide Records sufficient to show the number of individuals commissioned as special
police officers under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official Code § 5-129.02 (formerly § 4-114)
within the District of Columbia for each of the years 2023 through 2025.
FOIA G
Please provide Records sufficient to show the number of individuals whose commissions as special
police officers under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official Code § 5-129.02 (formerly § 4-114)
within the District of Columbia were renewed, suspended, or revoked, for each of the years 2023
through 2025, stated separately for each action.
FOIA H
Please provide all Records submitted to the DLCP related to the training that special police officers
commissioned under 6A DCMR § 1100.1 or D.C. Official Code § 5-129.02 (formerly § 4-114) are
required to complete.
FOIA I
Please provide copies of all Documents, including but not limited to the commission issued to each
special police officer, created or maintained by the DLCP in connection with applications submitted under 6A DCMR § 1103.3 by any individual or corporation seeking authorization for a
special police officer to carry a firearm, for the years 2023 through 2025.
FOIA J
Please provide all Records submitted to the DLCP related to the training that special police officers
are required to complete under 6A DCMR § 1103.3 to obtain or maintain authorization to carry a
firearm.
FOIA K
Records sufficient to show Your efforts to locate and produce the Records requested in FOIA A
through FOIA J above, including:
1. Where You searched for responsive Records and Documents.
2. Who searched for responsive Records and Documents.
3. Who was asked to produce responsive Records and Documents.
4. The identity of any Records and Documents that were located but not produced for any
reason.
INSTRUCTIONS
1. "Document" or "Documents" means any documents or electronically stored information of
any kind—including writings, drawings, graphs, charts, photographs, sound recordings,
images, and other data or data compilations—stored in any medium from which
information can be obtained either directly or, if necessary, after translation by the
responding party into a reasonably usable form.
2. "You" or "Your" means the District of Columbia Department of Licensing and Consumer
Protection, as successor to the former Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs
with respect to special police officers, and all of its attorneys, employees, officers, directors,
bureaus, offices, divisions, and subdivisions.
3. "DLCP" means the District of Columbia Department of Licensing and Consumer
Protection and all of its attorneys, employees, officers, directors, bureaus, offices, divisions,
and subdivisions. References to Records "created or maintained by," "received by," or
"submitted to" the DLCP also include Records created or maintained by, received by, or
submitted to the former Department of Consumer and Regulatory Affairs that are now in
the DLCP's possession, custody, or control.
4. 5. 6. 7. "Record" or "Records" means any documents or electronically stored information of any
kind—including writings, drawings, graphs, charts, photographs, video recordings, sound
recordings, images, databases, and other data or data compilations—stored in any medium
from which information can be obtained either directly or, if necessary, after translation by
the responding party into a reasonably usable form.
If You withhold any Record or information responsive to these requests, please identify
the Record or information in as much detail as possible and state specifically why each

title: Dolores Huerta

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Dolores Huerta
communications.communication:
Dear FBI:

This is a request for records under  the Freedom of Information Act. 

RECORDS REQUESTED

All records relating to farmworker activist and labor organizer Dolores Huerta (full name: Dolores Clara Fernández Huerta), born 10 April 1930 in Dawson, New Mexico, USA; died 28 October 2026.

PROOF OF DEATH

Ms. Huerta's obituary from the Associated Press is attached. 

CROSS-REFERENCE SEARCH

Please conduct a cross-reference search of the following subjects for additional records related to Ms. Huerta: 

1. Cesar Chavez (born Cesario Estrada Chavez on 31 March, 1927 in Yuma, Arizona; died 23 April 1993) https://www.nytimes.com/1993/04/24/obituaries/cesar-chavez-66-organizer-of-union-for-migrants-dies.html
2. Fred Ross Sr. (born 23 August 1910 in San Francisco, California; died 27 September 1992) https://www.nytimes.com/1992/10/02/obituaries/fred-ross-dies-at-82-farm-union-organizer.html
3. United Farm Workers
4. Community Service Organization
5. Agricultural Workers Association
6. National Farm Workers Association
7. Dolores Huerta Foundation
8. All other subjects whose files are likely to contain records related to Ms. Huerta.

SCOPE OF SEARCH

In addition to your standard search practices, please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) Indices, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies at FBI Headquarters. Please also conduct a search for records at the Alexandria Records Center. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing the transfer or destruction. If previously-released records are available, then I request a rolling release consisting of those records while additional records are located and processed.

FORM OF PRODUCTION

I would prefer that the Bureau produce responsive records electronically, by email attachment if available or on CD-ROM if not.

REQUEST FOR FEE WAIVER

I respectfully request that all fees related to this request be waived.

Public Interest Factors:

1. The subject of the request must concern identifiable operations or activities of the Federal Government. My request satisfies this factor because it seeks records created or maintained by the FBI.

2. The records must be likely to contribute to the understanding of the subject of the request. My request satisfies this factor because Ms. Huerta has recently died, meaning that the Bureau may now be able to release records that were not previously available via the FOIA/PA.

3. The disclosure must contribute to the understanding of the public—meaning a reasonably broad audience of persons interested in the subject—as opposed to the individual understanding of the requester. My request satisfies this factor because Ms. Huerta was a public figure and prominent activist. Thus, a broad audience of persons will likely be interested in the records I seek. I will also make any records available online for free via MuckRock.com.

4. The public's understanding must be enhanced by the disclosure to a significant extent. My request likely satisfies this factor because Ms. Huerta has recently died—meaning that the Bureau can now release responsive records that it could not have released until now.

Commercial Interest Factors

1. The existence and magnitude of a commercial interest: I have no commercial interest whatsoever in these records; I am just a curious American citizen with an interest in his government's surveillance of its critics. Thus, this factor cuts in favor of a fee waiver.

2. The primary interest in disclosure, i.e., whether disclosure is primarily in the commercial interest of the requester: I have zero commercial interest in disclosure, therefore the public interest outweighs my (nonexistent) private interest.

Conclusion: on balance, all of the Bureau's regulatory factors tilt decisively in favor of granting me a fee waiver. If you do decide to charge me fees, please notify me in advance if you anticipate that those fees will exceed $25.
